chat.text: reverse coa is in the RFC editor queue.  I will issue a new rev after the meeting

chat.text: Yes, please, join the queue

chat.author: Sri Gundavelli
chat.text: I thought 802.11bh allowing signaling of a stable Mac (securelly) to the AP.  Can that not be associated to dynamic Mac, and use stable Mac for policy?

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text:
@sri does that get sent in a RADIUS attribute? 
Or, does it need to be in a RADIUS attribute?

chat.author: Sri Gundavelli
chat.text: Alan - Sent in .11 messages; securly. AP can establish correlation to the current/rotated mac

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text: Thanks

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text: For Margarets  comments, I think this has similar security issues to CUI

chat.author: Jan-Frederik Rieckers
chat.text: If I read the slides correctly, the idea is to use client certificates and issue one client certificate per client and identify the client based on that.

chat.author: Alexander Clouter
chat.text: the rotation of the Persistent-Device-Id similarly to CUI should help

chat.author: Jan-Frederik Rieckers
chat.text: So it would basically be an identification of the client certificate, not the device, but the CA is designed to issue one certificate per device only.

chat.author: Alexander Clouter
chat.text: @janfred yes, particularly for EAP-TLS the device identity can from from something baked into the cert at enrollment

chat.author: Dan Harkins
chat.text: it's not equivalent of turning off MAC randomization. MAC randomization protects the STA from a passive observer on the 802.11 link tracking a device. But the STA can agree to let the RADIUS server track it. It still retains privacy over the air.

chat.author: Alexander Clouter
chat.text: similarly I think ultimately for example eduroam users do not "opt into" CUI

chat.author: Alexander Clouter
chat.text: ...it still gets set :)

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text: Maybe the sticking point is that CUI is unique per session, and Persistent-Device-ID is the same across multiple sessions?

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: If we already have CUI, and it does the same thing as this option, why not use CUI?

chat.author: Jan-Frederik Rieckers
chat.text:
CUI is supposed to be constant per Operator (Operator-Name) AFAIR.
I don't recall if it has an epoch or something like this.

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: The fact that we have one option for doing something I don't think we should do (identifying a specific device or user) doesn't mean it would be better to have 2.

chat.author: Alexander Clouter
chat.text: CUI can vary with time, I like to mix ISO week number (with year) into its generation

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text:
@margaret - only the RADIUS systems see the device ID.
The "on the wire" Wi-Fi packets don't change.  So the publicly visible MAC or IDs are still randomized

chat.author: Alexander Clouter
chat.text: CUI may be constant for _eduroam_, but it does not need to be

chat.author: Alexander Clouter
chat.text: (defined as a constant)

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: That is a great quality of CUI...  It can't easily be used to track a user between sites/sessions.  Does this identify _not_ have that property?

chat.author: Dan Harkins
chat.text: and there is significant value in having the publicly visible MAC remain randomized

chat.author: Alexander Clouter
chat.text: it does, they proposed on a slide you can mix in week number to rotate it over time

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: I agree, Dan. My question is:  Is there a good reason for creating something else that would identify the device.

chat.author: Alexander Clouter
chat.text: (epoch)

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: @Alan How do the RADIUS device see this in a way that is not available to anyone who can view the RADIUS/UDP traffic in transit?

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text: The solution is to get rid of RADIUS/UDP. :(

chat.author: Valery Smyslov
chat.text: And we worked on this solution here :-)

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: @Alan, I agree.  But, at this point, the majority of _countries_ do not support RadSec for subscriber institutions.

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: It will take years.

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text: this is likely to not be used for eduroam.  It's largely for enterprise

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: Devices do not really know whether they are on eduroam or some other network.

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: They don't treat the "eduroam" SSID specially.

chat.author: Jan-Frederik Rieckers
chat.text:
I think the point on the last slide is important:
"MUST strip identifier at admin-domain boundry"

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: What would this be good for that CUI isn't?

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: There are a lot of things that should be stripped at the admin domain boundary and are not...

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text: @margaret - the draft talks about enrolled devices.  So tracking corporate-owned devices is a reasonable thing for corporations to do

chat.author: Alexander Clouter
chat.text: @margaret one use case is if the machine is infected and trying to infect the rest of the network, a local admin may want to just block the device rather than all the devices of the user

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: RADIUS servers at the edge won't necessarily know this attribute exists, never mind that they  are required by some RFC to strip it.

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text: @margaret - yes, that's true.

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text: We seem to have lost the transcript

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: I am trying to come up with a list of attributes we should strip when proxying from RadSec to RADIUS/UDP, because someone may have sent them privately (in RadSec) and not realized they might be sent in RADIUS/UDP later.

chat.author: Lorenzo Miniero
chat.text: Transcript should be back

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text: thanks!

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: I am also wondering if we need an attribute for RadSec packets that says "don't procxy me to RADIUS/UDP"

chat.author: Alexander Clouter
chat.text: @margaret maybe easier just to have an allow list which is a subset of the RadSec allow list?

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: If that existed, maybe we could allow some attributes in RadSec only, and only if that attribute is also set?

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text:
@margaret - that's likely to be a "live" document for something like eduroam.
Maybe we can put a short list into the "Proxy best practices" document?

chat.author: Margaret Cullen
chat.text: An allow list is plausible...  I know people will want to send things in RadSec now that its secure to do so.

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text:
there are many, many, people who have "poached" on the 8-bit attribute space.  We can likely just propose this in the doc.
It's not likely that there will be another RFC which requests allocation of 191

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text:
the RADIUS registry is 
https://www.iana.org/assignments/radius-types
